text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The Competiion Council launched investigations in the case of the local Euro Trading Chemicals trading firm which aquired a majority stake in several chemical plants.
ADEVARUL
- The central bank might resume the announcement of the daily reference rate for national leu currency.
- The leu appreciated on the interbank market.
- State-run animal farms are seriously affected by a shortage of funds to buy fodder, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Shortage of funds force the Transport Ministry to give up 128 investment projects.
- The trade unions at the Craiova-based Daewoo Automobile Craiova ask for better wages.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Police continuies to investigate the alleged irregularities at the leading Bacorex SA commercial bank.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis starts official visit to Romania.
- The Constanta Black Sea port was closed on Wednesday following strong winds and storms.
ADEVARUL
- Health Ministry Stefan Dragulescu threatened to resign if the 1997 health budget does not amount to 4.0 percent of the GDP.
- Four hospitals in the central county of Brasov could be closed due to shortage of funds.
- Romania's former King Michael will try to win British support for Romania's NATO integration.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The opposition Party of Social Democracy asked for a meeting with President Emil Constantinescu to discuss what it called "authoritarian attitudes" allegedly adopted by the ruling coalitionin in parliament .
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
